 Order

This is first application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.96/2022 registered at Police Station - Malawar, District- Rajgarh for the offence under Sections 376(D), 506 of IPC.
The applicant is the mother-in-law of the prosecutrix.
She lodged the report on 09.05.2022 alleging that on 07.05.2022 her husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law had come to her house to take her in in-laws house.

On the way, mother-in-law stopped the vehicle and took the prosecutrix for urination, thereafter, her mother-in-law pushed the prosecutrix on the ground and father- in-law committed rape and thereafter her husband also came and committed rape against her will.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
There was a family dispute with the daughter-in-law and she was living separately.
The medical report also does not suggest any external injury on her.
If there was no struggle of rape on a rough surface.
On the date of incident the applicant alongwith her husband and son had gone to attend wedding ceremony, which is about 80 kms from the alleged spot of incident.
In this regard, a fast track receipt of toll plaza has been filed.

Considering the submission of the prosecutrix and medical report and the fact that the applicant is a lady and there is no possibility of her abscontion, I am of the view that prima facie case is made out for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant on the condition that the applicant will co-operate with the investigation and shall not tamper the evidence.
It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting officer.
The applicant shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in sub-section (2) of Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
A typed copy of this order is being forwarded to the Office of the Advocate General, on their email address, for intimation to the Police Station concerned.
Accordingly, the application is allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
